benchmarks.title: National Long COVID prevalence by survey wave, 2022-2024
benchmarks.why: Long COVID: national prevalence and health-center visits
benchmarks.how_to_use: Check a document's Long COVID prevalence or activity-limitation percentage against the survey waves of the same years; a match says the figure is plausible, not that the definitions are identical.

provenance.collection_note: Adults answering the online Household Pulse Survey; not clinically confirmed.
provenance.computed_by: Computed in code from the federal file; no AI model
provenance.relevance: Self-reported, not clinically confirmed, and not tied to a diagnosis code.
provenance.reliability: Published 95% intervals for every survey wave.

limits: Self-reported, not clinically confirmed, and not tied to a diagnosis code.
Adults 18 and over in the United States; the survey changed design between waves, so trend across phases is indicative only.

benchmarks.title: NAMCS Health Center visits with post-COVID-19 condition (ICD-10-CM U09.9) listed, 2024
benchmarks.why: Long COVID: national prevalence and health-center visits
benchmarks.summary: 2024: about 43,343 weighted health-center visits listed post-COVID-19 condition (ICD-10-CM U09.9) (169 sampled visits; meets the 30-record reliability floor).
benchmarks.how_to_use: Context or cross-check for a document that reports health-center or outpatient visit counts; never a national prevalence or a cost.

provenance.collection_note: Diagnoses recorded for a national sample of visits to community health centers; visits, not people.
provenance.computed_by: Computed in code from the federal file; no AI model
provenance.relevance: Community health centers only: not all outpatient care in the United States.
provenance.reliability: 169 sampled visits; meets the 30-record reliability floor.

limits: Community health centers only: not all outpatient care in the United States.
Counts visits, not people, and not dollars; one person can appear in several visits.

benchmarks.title: MEPS 2024: annual hours U.S. adults spend on health care time and paperwork
benchmarks.why: Fits this simulator's care fragmentation results
benchmarks.summary: own medical visits and filling prescriptions: 60.6 hours a year; medical visits and prescriptions for other people: 30.4 hours a year; paying or managing medical bills and insurance: 18.9 hours a year; health care paperwork: finding doctors, understanding plans, getting approvals: 15.5 hours a year; 15.9% of adults cared for someone in the past 30 days.
benchmarks.how_to_use: Context for administrative and care-navigation burden and for caregiving in any document; a general adult benchmark, never a Lyme or Long COVID figure.

provenance.collection_note: Respondent-reported conditions and hours, coded to ICD-10 by MEPS abstractors; not a clinical record.
provenance.computed_by: Computed in code from the federal file; no AI model
provenance.relevance: All U.S. adults who answered the questionnaire, not people with Lyme disease or Long COVID: MEPS cannot identify either condition reliably (AHRQ, 2026-09-24).
provenance.reliability: About 11,600 adults, design-based standard errors; about 6% skipped each time item.

limits: All U.S. adults who answered the questionnaire, not people with Lyme disease or Long COVID: MEPS cannot identify either condition reliably (AHRQ, 2026-09-24).
Fielded in 2024 only: the questionnaire was funded for that year, so there is no trend and no later update.
